transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-11
Start: 10:00 AM PST
Duration: 52 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Evelyn Park, Marcus Reed, Priya Nair, Jordan Lee, Samir Patel, Lena Morales, ~140 others (company all-hands)

Summary (auto): Quick leadership check-in focused on capacity, performance tradeoffs, hiring runway, and risk posture as we head into Q4. Longer Q&A than usual; several follow-ups assigned.

[00:00] Priya Nair: Good morning everyone, thanks for joining. I'll keep this tight — today's called "Holding Pattern to Velocity" because we have to talk about how we move from steady-state to the next push without burning runway. Evelyn, quick kickoff?

[03:30] Evelyn Park (CEO): Thanks Priya. Two big pieces: 1) we need predictable latency for a set of customers pushing to production and 2) we can't overspend on dedicated capacity before we have commit. So I want clear tradeoffs — where we accept slightly higher p95 for cost savings, where we don't. Also, hiring runway is on my mind.

[07:12] Marcus Reed (CFO): High level from finance — cash is fine but runway assumptions shift if we ramp Dedicated capacity aggressively. We're asking for modeled scenarios: best, base, and cautious. Please include commitment models and break-even points.

[10:45] Jordan Lee (VP Eng): Quick engineering snapshot — inference runtime improvements shipped last sprint (attention tiling, dynamic kernel selection) are down about 8-12% on token cost in our internal bench. But the variability at long sequences still bites. We also found a subtle KV cache eviction pattern that causes a throughput cliff when tail latency aligns with GC windows. Samir will talk more about remediation.

[14:02] Samir Patel (Director, Platform): Yeah, on that KV — we initially saw it as a K-V cash, like the cache was thrashing, but it's an edge case with our prefix caching and pre-warming behavior. Short term fix: adjust pre-warm thresholds and backoff on slot eviction. Mid-term: smarter shard placement and adaptive rekeying.

[17:30] Audience Q (internal): Are we moving customers to Dedicated if they hit p99 SLA misses? What is the play?

[21:00] Priya Nair: Playbook idea — priority routing. If hosted variant starts missing SLA, route to a compatible Dedicated pool or cheaper model variant with automatic fallback. We must codify which customers, what telemetry triggers, and the automated rollback. Jordan: can we detect this reliably?

[24:15] Jordan Lee: We have metrics — per-route token latency, queue depth, and KV hit rate. Combining them with a short-lived anomaly detector should be fine. But false positives are a risk; we need a two-step confirmation window before automated migration. Also, engineer ops burden: migrations must be transparent to customers or graceful degrade.

[28:00] Evelyn Park: On the product side, we need customer-facing comms templates — when we move a customer, we should provide a clear note: why, expected impact, and rollback details. Don't surprise enterprise legal.

[32:10] Lena Morales (VP People): Hiring update — offers accepted are slower; comp bands and interview velocity are in my notes. We should temporarily tilt hiring to infra/SRE for next 8 weeks to support the platform stabilization. Also holiday on-call rotations need coverage.

[36:05] Marcus Reed: If we shift hiring, update the model. Also consider contractor short-term for SRE spikes — cost vs time tradeoff.

[40:00] Audience Q: Any SOC/ISO/compliance impacts if we move customers between hosted and dedicated in different regions?

[44:30] Priya Nair: Important. If region or VPC controls are required, automated migration should not change data residency or contractual guarantees. For regulated customers, moves must be manual and flagged. Security team to add a gating check. Samir, add audit log hooks.

[48:00] Jordan Lee: On rollout cadence — propose a canary style: 5% traffic route, monitor 30m, expand to 25%, then full, with automatic rollback thresholds. Documented in the runbook and tied to the console alerts. This also helps cost smoothing.

[51:40] Priya Nair: Quick recap: Samir runs the Dedicated vs Hosted cost sim and bench details; Jordan authors the routing/canary playbook; Lena adjusts hiring priorities; I will circulate the capacity and runway slides. Expect the follow-ups in the next week. Big thanks — we have a bunch of Q&A feedback and some detailed notes in the shared doc (link: internal:/docs/hp-to-velocity-20261111).

End of meeting.

Notes on transcription quality: occasional mislabels ("K-V cash" for KV cache), punctuation and sentence joins where people cross-talk. Natural speech patterns: filler words (uh, so), truncated thoughts, and quick clarifications.

Referenced artifacts: internal deck (Q4 capacity + runway), preliminary stress spreadsheet (internal:/sheets/stress-20261110), routing/canary draft (internal:/playbooks/routing-canary-draft).

- Priya to send slide deck and link to the bench results by 2026-11-13.
- Samir to run 8xA100 stress run and produce a CSV with p50/p95/p99 and KV hit rates by 2026-11-20.
- Jordan to draft the routing + canary runbook and validate alert thresholds by 2026-11-17.
- Lena to update the hiring prioritization and publish an interim rota for on-call by 2026-11-18.
